literal: The fathers and others returned the government with earnest yielding; now I shall personally take the hundred affairs; return to your offices and bureaus—for separate disposition.
idiomatic: "My uncles have yielded the government with earnest care. I shall now personally hold the hundred affairs. Return to your offices; you will be dealt with separately."

literal: Soon an edict said: "I, few and dim, early met with bereavement; orphaned and alone in affliction, I do not know what to cross to.
idiomatic: Soon an edict said: "Orphaned and young, I met bereavement early and stand alone in grief, not knowing how to cross the flood."

literal: Truly I rely on the former emperor's sage virtue and the lingering grace he spread; the chief ministers are loyal and worthy and toil for the royal house—thereby able to comfort and harmonize above and below and make pure within and without.
idiomatic: "I rely on the former emperor's sage virtue and lingering grace, and on loyal ministers who toil for the house—by them above and below are harmonized and within and without made pure."

literal: Then I followed the model of returning the son and announced the return of government with yielding; the reasoning was earnest to the utmost and far away hard to wrest away.
idiomatic: "They followed the model of returning rule to the heir and announced their abdication with earnest pleas I could not wrest away."

literal: I shall now encourage this emptiness and deficiency and personally survey the machinery of affairs.
idiomatic: "I shall now rouse my own emptiness and personally oversee the machinery of state."

literal: King Zun, as eldest imperial uncle, his Way-nature deep and congealed, may advance to Grand Mentor and hold the Grand Commandant;
idiomatic: "King Zun, eldest imperial uncle, whose Way is deep and still, shall advance to grand mentor and hold the grand commandant;"

literal: Minister of Works Prince of Beihai, as youngest imperial uncle, bright and enlightened, fame and strategy flourishing in achievement, may be made Grand General and Recorder of the Masters of Writing."
idiomatic: "Minister of Works Prince of Beihai, youngest imperial uncle, bright in fame and strategy, shall be grand general and recorder of the Masters of Writing."

literal: After Shizong took government, Xi was uneasy in mind.
idiomatic: Once Shizong took the reins, Xi grew uneasy.

literal: Yet his state's purification officer Liu Xiaogou often said that those about the throne spoke of wishing to execute Xi.
idiomatic: His state's purification officer Liu Xiaogou kept saying that men about the throne meant to kill Xi.

literal: Xi heard and sighed: "I have not failed in heart—how should the imperial house be like this!
idiomatic: Xi heard this and sighed: "I have not betrayed them—how should the house treat me so!"

literal: Thereby he constantly harbored worry and fear.
idiomatic: From then on he lived in constant fear.

literal: Moreover Zhao Xiu held exclusive favor; kings and dukes rarely obtained audience.
idiomatic: Zhao Xiu held exclusive favor, and princes rarely saw the emperor.

literal: Xi thereupon with his consort's elder brother, concurrent Attendant of the Yellow Gate Li Boshang, plotted rebellion.
idiomatic: Xi then plotted rebellion with his consort's elder brother Li Boshang, who also served as attendant of the Yellow Gate.

literal: At that time Shizong was at Xiaoping Ford; Xi was in a small residence west of the city.
idiomatic: Shizong was then at Xiaoping Ford; Xi lay in a small house west of the city.

literal: At first he wished to drive the troops straight into the Metal Enclosure; the multitude harbored dismay and strangeness; Xi's heart thereby slackened.
idiomatic: At first he meant to march straight into the Metal Enclosure, but his men wavered and his heart slackened.

literal: From dawn reaching dusk, the plan could not be decided; then they agreed not to leak and dispersed.
idiomatic: From dawn to dusk he could not decide; at last they swore secrecy and dispersed.

literal: Prince of Wuxing Yang Jishi went out and at once galloped to report; yet Xi did not doubt.
idiomatic: Prince Jishi of Wuxing rode out at once to report him, yet Xi did not suspect.

literal: Then with concubines he went to the Hongchi villa; he sent Xiaogou to present a memorial, saying "inspecting fields and herds."
idiomatic: He went with his women to the Hongchi villa and sent Xiaogou with a memorial claiming he was "inspecting fields and herds."

literal: Xiaogou reached Mount Mang ridge and already met soldiers; they wondered at Xiaogou's red garments and were about to kill him.
idiomatic: Xiaogou reached Mount Mang ridge and met soldiers; struck by his red dress, they were about to kill him.

literal: Xiaogou in distress and urgency said he wished to report rebellion; then they eased him.
idiomatic: Pressed hard, Xiaogou said he meant to report treason, and they spared him.

literal: That night Xi lodged at Hongchi; great wind and violent rain uprooted trees and broke wood.
idiomatic: That night Xi slept at Hongchi while wind and rain uprooted trees.

literal: Xi did not know the affair was exposed.
idiomatic: Xi did not know the plot was exposed.

literal: That night someone said to Xi: "Your Highness gathered the multitude to plot the affair; seeing intent you stopped— I fear it will surely leak; this night how is it fitting to make yourself at ease?
idiomatic: That night someone told Xi: "Your Highness gathered men and halted when resolve faltered—the secret will leak. How can you rest easy tonight?"

literal: I fear peril and disaster are about to arrive.
idiomatic: "Disaster is near."

literal: Xi said: "Having this body and life, one should know to cherish oneself—how wait for others' words.
idiomatic: Xi said: "A man who values his life needs no one to tell him—he knows to save himself."

literal: Again it was said: "Your Highness's son's wife has already crossed the river; the two ends do not know each other—now bowing the brow in self-security, is it not perilous!
idiomatic: Another said: "Your son's wife has already crossed the river; the two ends cannot know each other—is bowing your head in false peace not perilous?"

literal: Xi said: "On the day I first sent her off I ordered her like a traveler crossing the river, to listen for my movements.
idiomatic: Xi said: "When I sent her off I told her to cross like any traveler and listen for my signal."

literal: Long ago I sent men to pursue her; by reckoning she should now have returned.
idiomatic: "I sent men after her long ago; by now she should be back."

literal: Yet Yin Wuqi and Xi's eldest son Tong had already entered Henei commandery, drawn up weapons, and released prisoners.
idiomatic: Yet Yin Wuqi and Xi's eldest son Tong had already entered Henei commandery, arrayed arms, and freed prisoners.

literal: And officers and soldiers everywhere pursued Xi.
idiomatic: Soldiers everywhere were already pursuing Xi.

literal: Xi himself fled southeast from Hongchi; servants did not pass a few persons; those left and right following Xi were only concurrent Defender of the Barrier Yin Longhu.
idiomatic: Xi fled southeast from Hongchi with only a few servants; of those who still followed him, only Defender Yin Longhu remained.

literal: Xi in distress and urgency did not know what to do; he said to Longhu: "I am muddled and cannot bear it—try making a riddle; I shall think to solve it, to release poisonous oppression.
idiomatic: Desperate and at a loss, Xi told Longhu: "I am too muddled to bear this—make a riddle; I'll solve it to ease this poison in my chest."

literal: Longhu suddenly recalled an old riddle saying: "Sleeping then both sleep, rising then both rise; greedy as wolf and jackal, booty does not enter self.
idiomatic: Longhu suddenly remembered an old riddle: "Sleep together, rise together; greedy as wolf and jackal, yet booty never enters oneself."

literal: Altogether he had no mind toward plotting assassination.
idiomatic: He had no thought of plotting against Xi.

literal: Xi also did not take it as satire on himself; thereupon he solved it saying: "This is the eye.
idiomatic: Xi did not take it as aimed at him and solved it: "That is the eye."

literal: Yet Longhu considered it chopsticks.
idiomatic: Longhu had meant chopsticks.

literal: Crossing the Luo water, they reached the Cypress Valley stockade; followers were only Xi's two maternal uncles and Longhu.
idiomatic: They crossed the Luo and reached Cypress Valley stockade with only Xi's two maternal uncles and Longhu.

literal: Looking back he said to Longhu: "Even a common fellow still has integrity and righteousness; act to take death for each other—you may urge your heart and make the same plan as dying with the Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: Xi turned to Longhu: "Even common men keep faith. Take death for each other—steel your heart and die with the grand commandant as I do."

literal: Longhu said: "Longhu is an eastern-field common man; meeting Your Highness's breadth and brightness, I was received at your left and right.
idiomatic: Longhu said: "I am a common man from the eastern fields. Your Highness took me in and kept me at your side."

literal: Now belonging to peril and hardship, I hate that I have no far-reaching plan to rescue and aid the sage body; if I share life with Your Highness, though dead it is still living.
idiomatic: "Now in peril I lack any grand plan to save the throne; yet to die with Your Highness is still to live."

literal: Before long Xi was seized and sent to the Hualin capital pavilion.
idiomatic: Soon Xi was seized and sent to the Hualin capital pavilion.

literal: Shizong personally questioned the source of the affair; he put a thousand-jin lock on Longhu; the Feathered Forest guarded him.
idiomatic: Shizong questioned him in person, put a thousand-jin lock on Longhu, and had the Feathered Forest guard him.

literal: Earlier, at Gaozu's leisure banquet, he said at ease to Xi and the others: "My later sons and grandsons may by chance not reach the mark; you observe the principle of assisting and taking over—let no other have it.
idiomatic: At a leisure banquet Gaozu had told Xi and the others: "My descendants may fall short; watch how you might assist and take the throne—let no outsider have it."

literal: At the end Xi, though his words were not in order, still wept and traced the former intent; yet in fear and compulsion he lost his will and could not be stirred to generous feeling.
idiomatic: At the end Xi spoke brokenly yet wept and recalled that command; but fear crushed him and he could not rise to any noble passion.

literal: When he took leave of the various younger sisters and princesses, he spoke of one or two beloved concubines.
idiomatic: Taking leave of his sisters and princesses, he spoke of one or two favorite concubines.

literal: The princess wept and cursed him: "Sitting in much taking of these maidservants, greedy in pursuit of goods, fearing crime you made rebellion, bringing about today's affair—why again entrust inquiry to such as these!
idiomatic: A princess wept and cursed him: "You hoarded these women, chased wealth, feared punishment, rebelled, and brought us here—why speak of them now!"

literal: Xi was ashamed and without words; then he was ordered to die at his private residence.
idiomatic: Xi was shamed into silence and ordered to die at his private house.

literal: His palace women sang: "Pitiable Prince of Xianyang—how could he err in his doing.
idiomatic: His palace women sang: "Pitiable Prince of Xianyang—how could he err so?"

literal: Gold bed and jade couch cannot sleep; at night he treads frost and dew.
idiomatic: "Gold bed and jade couch bring no sleep; at night he treads frost and dew."

literal: Luo waters deep and deep spread the banks long; travelers—how can they cross.
idiomatic: "Luo waters run deep and long; how can a traveler cross?"

literal: The song thereupon flowed to the lands south of the Yangtze; northerners in the south, though rich and noble, when string and pipe played it, none did not shed tears.
idiomatic: The song spread south of the Yangtze; northerners there, however rich, wept whenever pipes played it.

literal: Those who plotted together were executed in the tens; Xi was secretly buried on the northern Mang.
idiomatic: Dozens of co-conspirators were executed; Xi was secretly buried on Northern Mang.

literal: His sons' registry affiliation was cut off.
idiomatic: His sons were struck from the imperial registry.

literal: Xi's various daughters were given slight assets and maidservants; the remaining family wealth was all divided and bestowed on the two houses of Gao Zhao and Zhao Xiu.
idiomatic: Xi's daughters received only modest property and maids; the rest of his wealth went to Gao Zhao and Zhao Xiu.

literal: The remainder was bestowed on inner and outer hundred offices down to those outside the current; the many had more than a hundred bolts, the least down to ten bolts.
idiomatic: The remainder was distributed to officials inside and outside the capital, and even to exiles—some received more than a hundred bolts of silk, others as few as ten.

literal: Afterward, whenever Xi's sons lacked food and clothing, only Prince of Pengcheng Xie several times a year repeatedly gave relief.
idiomatic: Afterward, whenever Xi's sons lacked food or clothes, only Prince Xie of Pengcheng repeatedly sent relief through the year.

literal: Xi had eight sons.
idiomatic: Xi had eight sons.

literal: Eldest son Tong, style Tanhe.
idiomatic: His eldest son Tong styled Tanhe.

literal: Secretly entering Henei, Administrator Lu Xiu at first was of one mind with Tong; when he heard Xi had failed, then he killed him.
idiomatic: Tong stole into Henei; Administrator Lu Xiu had first sided with him, but when Xi fell he killed Tong.

literal: Tong's younger brother Yi, style Zhonghe.
idiomatic: Tong's younger brother Yi styled Zhonghe.

literal: Later, when amnesty came, he went to court and submitted a memorial asking to bury his father.
idiomatic: After an amnesty he came to court and begged leave to bury his father.

literal: Year after year he wept and petitioned; Shizong did not permit.
idiomatic: He petitioned in tears year after year; Shizong refused.

literal: Yi then with his younger brothers Chang and Ye fled to Xiao Yan.
idiomatic: Yi then fled with his brothers Chang and Ye to Xiao Yan.

literal: Yi and Chang were born of Lady Shentu.
idiomatic: Yi and Chang were born of Lady Shentu.

literal: Ye was born of Consort Li.
idiomatic: Ye was born of Consort Li.

literal: Yi's appearance was tall and strong, bearing and regulation observable; Yan greatly valued him and enfeoffed him Prince of Xianyang.
idiomatic: Yi was tall and imposing, his bearing striking; Yan prized him and made him Prince of Xianyang.

literal: Yi yielded to his younger brother of the principal line Ye; Yan did not permit.
idiomatic: Yi yielded to his younger full brother Ye; Yan refused.

literal: Later he was made General of Trustworthy Martiality and Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, garrisoning Yuzhou.
idiomatic: He was later made general of trustworthy martiality and inspector of Qing and Ji, garrisoning Yuzhou.

literal: Yi plotted to raise the province and enter the [Northern Wei] state; Yan transferred him.
idiomatic: Yi plotted to surrender the province to Wei; Yan transferred him.

literal: Chang was made Yan's Direct Companion General.
idiomatic: Chang became Yan's direct companion general.

literal: Yi's younger brother Xianhe and Chang's younger brother Shu, later also fled to Yan.
idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Xianhe and Chang's younger brother Shu later fled to Yan as well.

literal: Xianhe died in the lands south of the Yangtze.
idiomatic: Xianhe died in the south.

literal: Shu, style Xiuhe.
idiomatic: Shu styled Xiuhe.

literal: Fine in appearance, skilled in breathing exercises, and also possessing military strategy.
idiomatic: He was handsome, skilled in breath cultivation, and gifted in strategy.

literal: Yan especially treasured him; he was enfeoffed Prince of Wei commandery, later changed to Prince of Ye, several times made a commander, and spied on the border territories.
idiomatic: Yan especially favored him, made him Prince of Wei commandery, later Prince of Ye, and repeatedly used him on the borders.

literal: At that time Yangzhou surrendered to Yan; military strength was already numerous; Yan's general Zhan Sengzhen, fearing they would turn and differ, wished to kill them all.
idiomatic: When Yangzhou surrendered to Yan its troops were numerous; Yan's general Zhan Sengzhen, fearing defection, wished to kill them all.

literal: Shu because of family and state, then all were permitted to return.
idiomatic: Shu pleaded for house and realm, and they were all allowed to return home.

literal: Yan made Shu General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Ying Province.
idiomatic: Yan made Shu general who pacifies the west and Yingzhou inspector.

literal: When Erzhu Rong harmed the hundred offices, Shu heard it and then asked Yan to campaign against Rong.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong slaughtered the court, Shu asked Yan to campaign against him.

literal: Yan then supplied his soldiers and horses; he harassed the border lands.
idiomatic: Yan supplied troops and horses, and Shu raided the frontier.

literal: In the time of the Former Deposed Emperor he secretly held Qiao city.
idiomatic: Under the Former Deposed Emperor he seized Qiao city.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Chu he was ordered that Censor Commandant Fan Zihu be mobile office and lead the Inspector of Xuzhou, Grand Commander Du De, to attack him.
idiomatic: At Emperor Chu's accession Fan Zihu, censor commandant, was sent as mobile office with Xuzhou inspector and grand commander Du De to attack him.

literal: Shu defended the city and could not be taken down; Zihu sent Golden Grandee Zhang Anqi to persuade him; Shu then asked to surrender the city and return south; Zihu permitted this.
idiomatic: Shu held the city and could not be taken; Zihu sent Golden Grandee Zhang Anqi to negotiate. Shu asked to surrender the city and return south; Zihu agreed.

literal: Shu relied on the sworn agreement and made no war preparations; Du De raided him, seized Shu and sent him to the capital, confined him at Yongning Buddhist temple, and before long he was ordered to die.
idiomatic: Trusting the oath, Shu made no defense; Du De raided him, seized him, and sent him to the capital. He was confined at Yongning temple and soon ordered to die.

literal: In the time of Emperor Jing, his son Zhen, from Jiankang going to Ye, memorialized asking to bury Shu; this was permitted.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Jing his son Zhen came from Jiankang to Ye and asked to bury Shu; permission was granted.

literal: An edict posthumously made Shu Palace Attendant, commander of all military affairs in Qing, Xu, Yan, Yang, and Yu provinces, Grand Mentor, Duke of the State of Si, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Inspector of Yang Province.
idiomatic: An edict posthumously made Shu palace attendant, commander of Qing, Xu, Yan, Yang, and Yu, grand mentor, duke of Si, director of the Masters of Writing, and Yangzhou inspector.

literal: After Zhen had buried him, he returned to the lands south of the Yangtze.
idiomatic: After the burial Zhen returned south.

literal: Ye, style Shimao.
idiomatic: Ye styled Shimao.

literal: Yan enfeoffed him Prince of Sanggan and made him Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: Yan made him Prince of Sanggan and regular attendant.

literal: He died at Moling.
idiomatic: He died at Moling.

literal: Earlier, in the Zhengguang era an edict said: "Zhou's virtue was lofty and thick; Cai Zhong enjoyed the state;
idiomatic: Earlier, in the Zhengguang era an edict said: "Zhou's virtue was deep and generous; Cai Zhong kept his state;"

literal: Han's Way was humane and forgiving; Huainan completed his kingship.
idiomatic: "Han's way was humane; Huainan finished as king."

literal: All were thereby to extend grace to beloved kin, wash away old guilt, righteousness manifest in former leaves, sung and flowing in histories before.
idiomatic: "All extended grace to kin, washed away old guilt, and left their mercy sung in former histories."

literal: Recently Prince of Xianyang and Prince of Jingzhao brought calamity on themselves; the affair arose from being misled between, yet there is still what may be pitied.
idiomatic: "Recently the princes of Xianyang and Jingzhao brought ruin on themselves through delusion, yet something in them still merits pity."

literal: Sons of both gates all may be permitted to attach to the registry.
idiomatic: "Sons of both houses may reattach to the registry."

literal: Later Xi's princely rank was again restored; he was buried with princely rites.
idiomatic: Later Xi's princely rank was restored and he was buried with princely honors.

literal: An edict made Ye's younger brother Tan inherit, changed enfeoffment to Prince of Fucheng, fief of eight hundred households.
idiomatic: An edict made Ye's younger brother Tan succeed, enfeoffed as Prince of Fucheng with eight hundred households.

literal: Tan was arrogant, fierce, and coarse; his father's younger brother Prince of Anfeng Yanming reproached him: "Your fierce perversity grows with your body; in former times Prince of Donghai in Song, Yi, was by nature in nature vulgar and inferior—men of the time called him 'Donkey Prince'; I have closely watched what you do and fear you too will not escape the donkey name."
idiomatic: Tan was arrogant and brutal; his uncle Prince Yanming of Anfeng rebuked him: "Your fierce nature grows with your body. Once Prince Yi of Eastern Sea in Song was so base that men called him Donkey Prince. Watching you, I fear you will earn the same name."

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuang he returned to his original enfeoffment.
idiomatic: At Emperor Zhuang's accession he recovered his original fief.

literal: In the Wuding era he was made Grand Mentor.
idiomatic: In the Wuding era he was made grand mentor.
